correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real distributional BV inputs, express Df as a finite signed measure and f modulo a constant as an integral of jumps. The explicit response K_alpha has integrated L1 absolute norm E_alpha(s). Tonelli gives the universal bound, attained by one jump. Strict concavity of E_alpha gives the precise unique location and interior equality cases. Evaluating at s=1/2 and differentiating proves unique optimal alpha=1/2. Since binary entropy has second derivative at most -4, the global measure-weighted quadratic error deficit follows; near-midpoint single jumps prove coefficient 1 optimal. CHECKER.py independently tested 18 jump integrals, 420 signed multijump cases, 101 mixture weights, endpoint/reflection and sharp stability. Numerical tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: Selecting a left versus right prefix/suffix averaging policy is a natural choice for reconstructing discontinuous real data. The exact minimax value log(2)/2 differs nontrivially from 1/e of either direction, and the unique optimal balance is not implied by the separate endpoint constants. The sharp quantitative BV stability estimate determines how close the variation measure must be to the unique worst jump location in near-extremizing signals. This is a motivated operator-design invariant, not a renamed one-sided Hardy estimate.
